text: Maiden Castle is a British mythological site in Dorset. A great hillfort was built there during the Iron Age, presumably by the Celts, on top of an earlier structure used by pre-Celtic people. In the fourth century the invading Romans capped the hill with a temple to Diana. The site has been held sacred for as much as 6,000 years. It may have been devoted to a wildwood goddess, if the Roman designation follows that of earlier peoples. Koch records it as one of Britain's largest hillforts, 3 km south-west of Dorchester in south Dorset, the main settlement of the Durotriges in the later pre-Roman Iron Age. Sir Mortimer Wheeler first excavated the site in 1934-7, and Niall Sharples excavated again in 1985.
